1.pericope_label: Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up. After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up
debates: Whether the two days and the third point to the resurrection of Christ
Whether the following on to know is a condition or a promise
Whose voice speaks the opening call
outliers: Ellicott calls the resurrection reading far-fetched over-refinement without New Testament warrant
Calvin declines a sense he admits is not unsuitable, on the ground that it is too refined
Gill points out that the conditional word is not in the original at all
themes: A prophet striking while the iron is hot
A surgeon binding the bone he has set
Mercy named as the thing that makes fear possible
Eyes lifted to a light that seems already out

4.pericope_label: O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away
debates: Whether the received text of the last clause is sound
Whether the goodness meant is their piety or their kindness to themselves
How God can be represented as at a loss
outliers: Clarke describes justice and mercy as each prevented in turn by the same people
Clarke and Ellicott independently emend the same letter in the closing clause
Calvin lays down a rule that promises among threats belong only to the remnant
themes: A cloud that promises rain and gives none
Goodness that cannot be said to have been done at all
A hard wedge fetched for a hard knot
A word that is food to some and a sword to others

6.pericope_label: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. But they like men have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me
debates: Whether the comparison is with Adam, with earlier generations, or with the nations
Whether sacrifice is rejected in itself or only when heartless
Whether the there of the last clause names a place or an occasion
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch insists the rejection falls on heartless sacrifice, not sacrifice as such
Ellicott passes on a proposal that the name Adam stands for the nations outside Israel
Calvin makes the corrupting of the worship itself the breach of the covenant
themes: Rites accumulated until God is thought to owe something
A commandment broken in a garden and a covenant broken in a land
Sacred tokens used to cover the breach they were meant to seal
Knowledge that reaches the affections and not only the mind

8.pericope_label: Gilead is a city of them that work iniquity, and is polluted with blood. And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way by consent
debates: Whether the disputed word means by consent or toward Shechem
Which Gilead is meant and why it is singled out
Whether open murder is charged or something less visible
outliers: Calvin says the particular charge against Gilead is now lost to us through the gaps in history
Calvin flatly denies that a place-name is intended and calls the reading a mistake
Clarke has the priests keeping the roads to stop worshippers reaching Jerusalem
themes: A city of refuge turned into an ambush
A heap raised as a witness and worshipped instead
Priests set to carry a torch before the people
Robbers not infamous among men but before God

10.pericope_label: I have seen an horrible thing in the house of Israel: there is the whoredom of Ephraim, Israel is defiled. Also, O Judah, he hath set an harvest for thee, when I returned the captivity of my people
debates: Whether the harvest set for Judah is a threat or a promise
Whether the word means a harvest or a planting
Who is the subject of the verb in the last verse
outliers: Ellicott finds the reciter’s hesitation marked in the pointing of the text
Calvin objects that the received rendering puts a third-person verb into the second
Clarke notes that Judah returned from captivity but the greater part of Israel never did
themes: A word that makes the hair stand on end
Good intention set up as a queen over heaven and earth
A sickle already thrust into the standing corn
A physician looking for one sound part and finding none
